name: showreel-27-keyboard

voice.text: Why does your form show the wrong keyboard? A text field opens the letter keyboard, so you hunt for the numbers. The fix: input mode, numeric. Now one tap opens the number pad, and the code goes straight in.

caption:
Why does your form show the wrong keyboard? 📱

A plain text field gets the phone's standard letter keyboard (inputmode="text" is the default), so for a one-time code, a PIN or an amount your user has to switch layouts and hunt for the digits. Add inputmode="numeric" and the phone opens a number pad: digits 0-9, one tap each. It only changes the keyboard, not what counts as valid, so keep your own checks. For emails and phone numbers use type="email" and type="tel". Chrome 66+, Firefox 95+, Safari 12.1+ (iOS 12.2+).
Save it for your next sign-up or checkout form, or send it to whoever builds yours.

sources.note: MDN inputmode: hints at the type of data so the browser can show an appropriate virtual keyboard; text (default) = standard keyboard for the locale; numeric = numeric keyboard, only digits 0-9; it does not enforce validity
inputmode: Chrome 66, Firefox 95 (Android 79), Safari 12.1, Safari iOS 12.2 (Edge follows Chrome)

tip.title: Why does your form show the wrong keyboard?
tip.why: A plain text field gets the standard keyboard for the user's locale (inputmode="text" is the default, MDN), so a code or PIN field opens letters and the user has to hunt for the digits. inputmode="numeric" asks the phone for a numeric keyboard with the digits 0-9. It changes only the keyboard, not validation.
